page: Microsoft Azure D8ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on ARM architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is equipped with an ARM Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz, offering 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs with 1 thread per core. Memory allocation totals 32.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per core. The CPU features 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware-accelerated AES cryptographic support. The server includes no dedicated GPU accelerators and no bundled local storage, requiring remote storage attached via Azure Premium Storage capabilities.

Benchmark measurements indicate consistent mid-tier compute capabilities across core synthetic suites, registering a single-core stress-ng metric of 2075.09 and a multi-core score of 16570.32. Geekbench testing yields 1693.0 in single-core and 9460.0 in multi-core routines, with Clang software compilation reaching 14408.0. Compression performance is robust, with single-threaded gzip throughput ranking in the top 25% at 33.17 GB/sec. Memory subsystem evaluation is strong, demonstrated by a top 10% PassMark memory score of 3116.62 and large-block read bandwidth of 168.63 GB/sec.

Performance tradeoffs emerge in specialized compute and machine learning domains. The PassMark encryption test ranks in the bottom 25% at 1504.14, and large language model prompt processing on a 7B model drops to the bottom 10% at 12.34 tokens/sec. The absence of x86 vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX limits matrix-heavy routines. However, the dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores and efficient cache hierarchy deliver reliable throughput for multi-threaded general workloads, web serving at 15.84 GB/sec, and in-memory caches, achieving 16.64 million Redis SET operations per second.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of the D8ps_v6 stems from its ARM Neoverse-N2 infrastructure, delivering predictable dedicated core compute and high memory throughput without the hypervisor thread contention found in simultaneous multithreading (SMT) designs. Workloads that match this profile include containerized microservices, Clang and GCC build pipelines, mid-scale database operations, in-memory caching layers, and general-purpose enterprise application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D8ps_v6 is an ARM-based general-purpose virtual machine powered by an 8-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per core, 32.0 GB of system memory, and a 128 MB L3 cache, operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides no bundled local storage or GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached Premium Storage. Benchmark tests demonstrate competitive memory throughput, earning a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3116.62 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 33.17 GB/sec. General multi-core processing, static web serving at 15.84 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations at 16.64 million operations/sec perform within median industry tiers, offset by lower throughput on complex encryption tests and 7B LLM prompt processing. The instance is well-matched for web serving, CI/CD compilation pipelines, caching infrastructure, and standard database services.
